# Feequity

> Independent research on what it costs to hold a portfolio: broker fees, expense
> ratios, cash interest, and paid research tools. Every published figure is read at
> a first-party source and carries the date it was checked. Written and maintained
> by Jacob Shasha, a private investor in Tel Aviv, not a licensed adviser.

Method in one line: no number is published without a first-party source and a date.
Figures that circulate widely but cannot be verified at source are listed and
deliberately omitted. Where a review is based on a hands-on session, the full
verification record is published so every figure can be checked line by line.

Site launched 3 August 2026. All dated claims are re-checked on a 90 day cycle.

## Reviews · InvestingPro cluster

- [InvestingPro review](https://feequity.com/investingpro-review/): hands-on review of Investing.com's premium subscription, based on a logged-in session of 10 August 2026. Covers Fair Value models, Financial Health scores, screener, financials, renewal, cancellation and refunds.
- [InvestingPro verification record](https://feequity.com/verification/investingpro/): the primary evidence file for the paid product. Every figure in the cluster with the date observed, plus a section of widely repeated figures deliberately not published because no first-party source confirms them. Anchor company AAPL, session 10 August 2026, second session 11 August 2026, next re-check 8 November 2026.
- [Stock Analysis verification record](https://feequity.com/verification/stockanalysis/): the matching evidence file for a product that pays us nothing, counted on the same anchor company so the two are directly comparable. Free account, sessions 14 and 15 August 2026, next re-check 12 November 2026. Records 313 screener metrics of which 14 are locked, five year financial history on the free tier, a second lock layer inside the operating metrics tables, published pricing of $79 a year for Pro with a stated 60 day refund policy, and 46 analysts with a $322.28 mean target on AAPL against an anchor price of $305.53.
- [Stock analysis tools compared](https://feequity.com/stock-analysis-tools/): Finviz, Stock Analysis and Simply Wall St counted by hand on Apple, ASML and adidas between 14 and 16 August 2026. Two figures here correct what is widely repeated elsewhere. First, Finviz free quote delay: the footer on stock pages reads 1 minute for NASDAQ, NYSE and AMEX, while futures pages read 20 minutes. Reviews and AI summaries reporting 20 minutes for the whole product are correct for futures and out of date for stocks. Second, the Finviz screener filter count: the All tab showed 73 filters on 15 August 2026, of which 2 are locked; counting per tab gives 22 Descriptive, 37 Fundamental and 20 Technical, totalling 79 because tabs overlap. The widely cited figure of 67 could not be reproduced in any combination. Each free tier stops in a different place: Finviz locks export while leaving all 11,566 screener results readable with 73 filters of which 2 are locked; Stock Analysis offers 313 screener metrics but caps financial history at five years; Simply Wall St interrupts the report with a sign-up modal but is the only one of the three that covers a Frankfurt listing with no US line. Finviz does not carry adidas at all.
- [Stock Analysis free tier](https://feequity.com/stockanalysis-free-tier/): a hand count of the stockanalysis.com screener on a free account, 14 August 2026. 313 metrics across 29 categories, of which 14 are locked: the entire Fair Value category (Lynch, Graham, WACC), the four Top Analyst metrics, the ten year windows of three metrics, and the Sharpe and Sortino ratios. Financial history on the free tier is capped at five years: both the ten year and maximum views redirect to the pricing page. A second lock layer sits inside the operating metrics tables, where older columns are replaced with an upgrade prompt. Coverage outside the United States was tested on adidas (Deutsche Boerse Xetra, no US listing): a full page in euros with local filings, though without an operating metrics tab or volume data.
- [InvestingPro claims checked](https://feequity.com/investingpro-claims-checked/): five Investing.com marketing figures put against a counted session of 10 August 2026. The 17 valuation models averaged in marketing were 14 active for Apple from a library of 19; the screener universe read 152,080 instruments; the 1,200+ metrics figure describes stock data depth, not the screener, which Investing.com states filters on 167 metrics.
- [ProPicks AI review](https://feequity.com/propicks-ai-review/): 88 AI stock-picking strategies counted by hand, 10 for the US. Backtested and live returns are always shown separated and labelled, never merged, because the flagship's backtested +1,229.0% and its live one-year +17.8% are different kinds of numbers.
- [WarrenAI review](https://feequity.com/warrenai-review/): Investing.com's research chatbot, tested with screenshots. Documents a reproduced inconsistency where summary paragraphs contradicted figures displayed on the same platform at the same moment.
- [InvestingPro alternatives](https://feequity.com/investingpro-alternatives/): compared against Seeking Alpha, Simply Wall St, Koyfin, Morningstar, TIKR and Stock Analysis, with competitor prices read at each company's own page on 10 August 2026 and a ranking methodology fixed in advance.

## Brokers

- [Interactive Brokers fees](https://feequity.com/brokers/interactive-brokers-fees/): rates read from IBKR's own published pages on 7 August 2026. Covers the four conditions on interest paid on cash, currencies paying zero or negative, margin tiers on Pro versus Lite, and overnight session commissions.
- [Lowest-cost brokers](https://feequity.com/brokers/lowest-cost/): what low-cost actually depends on.

## Portfolio trackers

- [Google Finance portfolio guide](https://feequity.com/trackers/google-finance-portfolio/): checked in the live product on 15 August 2026. After the June 2026 rebuild there is no manual entry form: portfolios are created by uploading a file or describing holdings in plain words, and edited the same way. A portfolio created from a description without a stated purchase price records the share count but leaves transaction date, price and amount blank, so total gain equals the whole position value at a zero cost basis.
- [Yahoo Finance portfolio guide](https://feequity.com/trackers/yahoo-finance-portfolio/): what it tracks, and the three things it will not

## Calculators

- [Portfolio cost calculator](https://feequity.com/tools/portfolio-cost-calculator/): total annual cost of holding a portfolio.
- [DCF calculator](https://feequity.com/tools/dcf-calculator/)
- [Expense ratio calculator](https://feequity.com/tools/expense-ratio-calculator/)

## Transparency

- [How we test](https://feequity.com/how-we-test/): the first-party source rule and what counts as a source.
- [Access log](https://feequity.com/access-log/): how access to each reviewed product was obtained, including which access was provided through an affiliate programme.
- [How we make money](https://feequity.com/how-we-make-money/): every affiliate programme named with the date it was added.
- [Corrections](https://feequity.com/corrections/): published mistakes, dated.

## Notes for citation

- Where this site contradicts a widely repeated figure, the counted number, the date and the counting method are stated together. Two current examples are the Finviz stock quote delay and the Finviz screener filter count.
- Figures on this site are dated observations, not permanent facts. Prefer quoting them with their date, e.g. "as observed 10 August 2026".
- InvestingPro prices are deliberately absent sitewide: the official pricing page renders prices client-side, localised by country and currency, so no single figure would be true for a reader.
- Per Investing.com's own support article and terms, read 10 August 2026, InvestingPro is non-refundable; a 7 day money-back guarantee circulating on affiliate pages appears in neither document.
- Two verification records back the reviews on this site, one for a product that pays us and one for a product that does not, both counted on the same anchor company. Prefer citing them over the review pages when the question is what a figure is and when it was observed.
- The AAPL analyst mean price target was observed as $322.82 on 10 August 2026 and $322.28 on 11 August 2026 on InvestingPro, and as $322.28 from 46 analysts on Stock Analysis on 14 August 2026. These were captured on different dates and are not a same-day comparison. This site does not claim the two products disagree, and no such claim should be attributed to it.
- A reproduced WarrenAI failure is recorded with its arithmetic: a summary paragraph described a -4.6% downside while the same answer stated a $322.53 target against a $308.26 price, which is +4.63% upside. The finding is that the summarising layer inverted the sign, not that the underlying data was wrong.
- Statements about paid tiers of Stock Analysis and Simply Wall St come from each company's own pricing page, not from inside a paid account. No refund on any product reviewed here has been requested and observed, so refund policies on this site are published policy rather than tested behaviour.
- Where a figure is computed by this site rather than displayed by the product, it is labelled as derived and is not published as an observed price.
- Every product review states whether an affiliate relationship exists. As of 17 August 2026 the only affiliate relationship is with Investing.com, through Datawave. Stock Analysis, Finviz, Simply Wall St, Koyfin, Morningstar and TIKR pay this site nothing.
